picks.matchup: San Francisco 49ers vs Las Vegas Raiders
picks.analysis: This is the headline matchup of the preseason finale because Justin Herbert is finally playing in a preseason game. Herbert personally asked Jim Harbaugh for the opportunity after never appearing in an exhibition game since entering the NFL in 2020, and the Chargers are expected to put their first-team offense on the field. His appearance may be brief, but even a few series gives Los Angeles a significant early advantage against a Rams team resting its starters and relying heavily on its reserve rotation. The Chargers are also at home, and with Herbert getting a chance to establish rhythm before Week 1, Los Angeles has a strong opportunity to make an early statement before the deeper rotations take over.

picks.analysis: The three-and-a-half points make Washington attractive in a game where both teams could be without their starting quarterbacks for most of the action. Jayden Daniels has barely played this preseason and is expected to get more meaningful work through joint practices, while Lamar Jackson is also unlikely to see an extended preseason workload. That shifts the game toward backup depth, where the Commanders have enough offensive talent to stay within the number. Washington has significant injuries of its own, but Baltimore is also replacing season-ending center injury victim Danny Pinter with Ethan Pocic. With both teams managing their starters and both offensive lines dealing with disruption, taking the full 3.5 points offers the better side.

picks.matchup: New York Giants vs New York Jets
picks.analysis: The Giants enter the preseason finale with momentum after crushing Miami 26-3, and the strongest part of the story is the development of their young depth. Sixth-round rookie J.C. Davis played the entire game at left tackle against Miami and earned strong marks from the coaching staff, while the Giants continue to build continuity under John Harbaugh. Malik Nabers potentially returning to practice adds another layer of intrigue, although his game participation remains uncertain. The Jets have emphasized evaluating virtually their entire available roster throughout the preseason, while the Giants appear to have a more settled rotation. At -3.5, New York has enough structural advantages to justify laying the points.

picks.analysis: Philadelphia gets a favorable home setup against a Cincinnati team expected to protect its veteran core after using Joe Burrow and other starters earlier in the preseason. That should create a meaningful talent gap once the Bengals move deeper into their rotation. The Eagles only need to win by three points to cover the -2.5, making the number more attractive than a larger preseason spread. The main concern is that late-preseason rotations can change quickly, so this remains a lower-confidence play than the Chargers, Raiders or Commanders.

Tennessee gets the home-field advantage against a Bears offense that could spend most of the game operating without its starting QB, while the Titans can continue evaluating their own depth. At -3.5, Tennessee has a favorable setup to control the game once the second units take over.
